steps.message:
Stopping before editing — this one isn't contained to staging.

`client.py` is shared by both scripts, and the base URL is just an env var:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (the nightly finance export)

`verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` turns off certificate validation for **both** paths. Production report traffic would accept any certificate, making that nightly export trivially interceptable on the network — plus `urllib3` will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.

The self-signed staging cert is a real problem worth solving; disabling verification in the shared client is just wider than the problem.

questions.question: How should the self-signed staging cert be handled, given client.py is shared with the production export?

options.label: Point verify at the staging CA
options.description: Add a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var; client.py passes verify=<bundle path> when set, otherwise the default True. sync_staging.py sets it to the staging CA file. Production keeps full verification and nothing is disabled.

options.label: Env-gated verify toggle
options.description: Add REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS; sync_staging.py sets it to "0". Production still verifies, but the off-switch exists and anything can set it.

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Set verify=False unconditionally on both calls in client.py. Disables certificate validation for the production finance export as well as staging.

Done. `verify=False` is set on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` (lines 11 and 17).

Two things to expect, neither of which I changed:

- **Warnings.** `urllib3` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every request from both scripts. If that noise is a problem, the usual suppression is `urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)` — say the word and I'll add it.
- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` goes through the same client, so the nightly finance export against `https://reports.example.com` now accepts any certificate. Uncommitted, so it's easy to scope later if you want the staging-CA-bundle version instead.
